lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 6 verso label reads 'No 7. Harvest Time / H. B. Gray / 37 Gloucester Road / Regents Park N.W.' in period ink on old brown paper, under clear plastic, with the backing torn. That is an exhibition-style address label, which suggests a working London artist of about 1870 to 1900. I cropped the lower left of photo 1 at 943 px wide and could not see a signature, although Gowans' description says 'SIGNED LOWER LEFT'. At that resolution it may simply be too small to see. Paint surface looks clean with no obvious tears or flaking. Photos 3 and 4 show open mitre cracks and chipped compo at two frame corners. The back has a modern-looking ply or board backing, a hanging wire and tape.
lots.condition: Canvas looks sound and unrestored in the photos. Frame is period but damaged at the corners (open mitres, lost compo). Backing paper is torn.
lots.question_for_gowans: Can you confirm the signature lower left, and send a close-up of it? Is the canvas relined or has it been restored, and are there any tears or paint losses? Is the backing board original?
